meta.title: OpenKortex · the second brain you host yourself
meta.description: Drop web pages, PDFs, videos, voice memos and meetings into one inbox. OpenKortex summarizes, tags and links them with your own AI keys and keeps everything as plain Markdown on your server. Open source under AGPL-3.0.
nav.label: Main
hero.title: Drop it in. Find it sorted.
hero.lead: OpenKortex is a second brain you run yourself. Web pages, e-books, recipes, photos, voice memos, meetings and prompts land in one inbox. Your own AI keys turn them into summaries, tags and links, kept as plain Markdown on your server.
hero.note: The demo runs in your browser with sample data. No account, no server, no AI.
orbit.label: Every app sends what you capture to your OpenKortex server, which files it as Markdown in your folder and answers your AI agents.
principles.label: Principles
p1.title: Your notes are files.
p1.text: Every entry is Markdown with YAML frontmatter, mirrored to a folder on your computer. Open it in any editor, today or in twenty years.
p2.title: Your server, your keys.
p2.text: There is no OpenKortex cloud. It runs where you install it and only calls the AI providers you give a key to.
p3.title: Your agents are welcome.
p3.text: A built-in MCP server lets Claude and other agents search, read and save, with a token you can revoke at any time.
flow.title: From drop to answer
flow.lead: What happens after you press capture.
s1.title: Capture
s1.text: Share from your phone, clip in the browser, press Alt+Space on Windows or let the meeting recorder listen. It all lands in one inbox.
s2.title: Sort
s2.text: In the background, OpenKortex transcribes, summarizes and pulls out tasks and people. Each entry gets tags and a folder. What you placed by hand stays put.
s3.title: Connect
s3.text: Wiki links, backlinks and objects for people, projects and ideas tie entries together. The graph shows what belongs with what.
s4.title: Ask
s4.text: Ask in your own words. The copilot answers from your notes and shows every source it used.

sc3.title: Agents read your brain, and write to it
sc3.text: The MCP server gives Claude and other agents the same knowledge you have. They search and read before they answer, and they save what they worked out as normal entries, right next to yours.
sc3.a: Six tools: search, read, save, organize, tasks, memory
sc3.b: What an agent writes is Markdown like everything else
sc3.c: One token per agent, revoked with a click

own.title: Nothing to escape from
own.lead: Your whole brain exists as a folder of Markdown files. OpenKortex is one way to work with that folder, not the place it is locked in.
own.f1t: Every entry is one .md file with YAML frontmatter. Links are [[wiki links]], tags are text. No export step, no proprietary format.
own.f2t: The server needs no app in front of it. The MCP server and the Markdown sync run on their own; use every app, one, or none.
own.f3t: Copy the folder to another computer, another server or another tool. A new OpenKortex server reads it back in.
own.f4t: Switch the server off tomorrow and the folder still opens in Obsidian, in VS Code or in a plain text editor.

faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.lead: The short version. The details are in the repository.
faq.a1: A second brain you host yourself. Everything you capture from the web, your phone, your desktop or your agents lands in one inbox and is summarized, tagged and linked by AI, then kept as Markdown.
faq.a2: Yes. OpenKortex is free software under the AGPL-3.0. You pay only for your own server and for what your AI providers charge for the keys you add.
faq.q3: Do I need an AI key?
faq.a3: Not to start. Without a key, capturing and writing work. Summaries, search by meaning and the copilot need one key from Anthropic, OpenRouter or Eden AI.
faq.a4: On the server you install it on: Postgres for the app, plus a two-way mirror as Markdown files in a folder on your computer. There is no OpenKortex cloud.
faq.q5: Can I take my notes elsewhere?
faq.a5: Any time. The Markdown folder is the export: copy it, open it in Obsidian or any editor, put it under Git, or read it into a new server.
faq.a6: Any client that speaks MCP, such as Claude. The built-in server offers six tools to search, read, save and organize, and each agent gets its own revocable token.
faq.a7: A web app for every browser, a Windows app, an Android app and a browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox. iOS is prepared in the code.
faq.a8: No. OpenKortex runs where you install it, from a laptop with Docker to a small server with your own domain.
faq.a9: Please do. Bug reports and ideas go into GitHub issues, code comes as a pull request with a signed contributor agreement.
